source.title: ISC 2026 Examination Specimen Question Paper, Biology Paper 1 (Theory), with Answer Key
source.subject: biology
source.authorityName: Council for the Indian School Certificate Examinations (CISCE)
source.session: Specimen Question Paper for the ISC 2026 Examination
source.extractionTool: pdftotext -enc UTF-8 (raw and -layout); tables and notation checked against pypdfium2 page renders
source.notes: Every page footer prints 'ISC (CLASS XII) SPECIMEN QUESTION PAPER 2026' (pages 1-11) and 'ISC (CLASS XII) SPECIMEN ANSWER KEY 2026' (pages 12-17), so examYear = 2026 (the examination year the specimen is for); the file was uploaded to cisce.org in 2025/08. The question paper (11 printed pages, PDF pages 1-11) is followed in the same PDF by its answer key (PDF pages 12-17); answerSourceUrl is the same URL. Maximum Marks 70, Time Allotted Three Hours plus fifteen minutes reading time; eighteen questions. Section A (20 marks): Question 1 (i)-(xviii), 1 mark each except (xv) and (xviii) which carry [2] and are split into (a) and (b) at the [1] each printed in the answer key. Section B: Questions 2-8, 2 marks each; Section C: Questions 9-15, 3 marks each; Section D: Questions 16-18, 5 marks each. Internal choice (one question in each of Sections B, C, D): Questions 2, 10 and 17, each entered as two alternatives sharing choiceGroup. Multi-part Section B-D questions with one bracket mark are kept as one entry. Counting one alternative per choice group the pack totals 70. Three official answers are diagrams only (1(vii) pyramid of numbers, 2(i) pyramid of energy, 15 age pyramids) and are omitted. Many questions depend on figures/graphs that are not reproduced; those are flagged and set LOW when unanswerable without the figure. Cognitive tags printed per sub-part (e.g. '(Recall)') are recorded only when all parts of an entry share one tag.
source.usage: Official CISCE publication, freely available on cisce.org; question text reproduced for study with attribution and a link to the original. Figures are not reproduced.

questions.text: Why are tendrils of vine (Vitis) and pea (Pisum) considered to be analogous organs?

officialAnswer.text: Tendrils of vine are modified stems and of pea are modified leaves or leaflets. They perform the same function – climbing and supporting the plants.

questions.text: Darwin’s finches are best example of adaptive radiation. Justify.
extractionIssues: Internal choice: alternative (i) of Question 10 (OR (ii)).

officialAnswer.text: Darwin on voyage on the ship H.M.S Beagle, Galapagos Island separated from mainland South America – 13 species of Ground finches found on different islands. questions.text:
A scientist is attempting to create a recombinant DNA molecule by combining a plasmid vector and a foreign DNA. A plasmid DNA and a linear DNA of the same size have a single site for the restriction enzyme EcoRI. When cut by the same RE and separated by gel electrophoresis, the plasmid shows one DNA band, and the linear DNA shows two bands.
(i) What causes the difference between the number of DNA bands generated from the plasmid and from the linear DNA?
(ii) What is the advantage of using agarose in gel electrophoresis?
(iii) How does EcoRI differ from an exonuclease?
extractionIssues: Parts carry different printed tags: (i) Analysis, (ii) Analysis, (iii) Recall; no single cognitiveLevel recorded.

officialAnswer.text: (i) Plasmid is circular, therefore when cut by RE it produces only one fragment, whereas the linear DNA is cut to release two fragments. (ii) Agarose is non-reactive and large pore size allows easier separation of fragments. (iii) EcoRI is an endonuclease, it cuts the specific inner bonds while exonucleases cut outer bonds starting either from 3’- terminus or from 5’-terminus.

questions.text:
During a field excursion, a group of class XII students visited Kaziranga National Park and observed efforts to protect the Indian rhinoceros in its natural habitat. They also toured a botanical garden and a gene bank, where they saw endangered plant species and preserved seeds.
Based on this context, answer the following questions:
(i) Name and define the two types of conservation methods mentioned above.
(ii) What is cryopreservation?
(iii) Is Captive breeding an ex-situ or an in-situ strategy. Justify your answer with a reason.
extractionIssues: Notation rebuilt from the page render: '-196°C' (text layer '-1960C', printed with a superscript 0); check against the PDF.
Marks not itemised across (i)-(iii) (only [5] printed); kept as one entry.
Parts carry different printed tags: (i) Understanding, (ii) Recall, (iii) Evaluate; no single cognitiveLevel recorded.

officialAnswer.text: (i) (In-situ and ex-situ conservation methods respectively. In-situ conservation is the conservation of biotic resources in their natural habitats. Ex-situ conservation is the conservation of threatened species outside their natural habitats. (ii) Cryopreservation is in vitro conservation of tissues, organs, embryos, seeds etc. at low temperature of -196°C. (iii) Captive breeding is ex -situ conservation method because threatened and endangered species are bred and reared in zoological parks under human supervision

questions.text:
(a) Write a brief note on Griffith’s experiment. What was the conclusion drawn from this experiment?
(b) Name the parts ‘A’ and ‘B’ of the transcription unit shown below.
extractionIssues: Internal choice: alternative (i) of Question 17 (OR (ii)).
Figure on page 10 (transcription unit with parts A and B) not reproduced; part (b) cannot be answered without it.
Notation rebuilt from the page render: '60°C' (text layer '600C'); check against the PDF.
Parts carry different printed tags: (a) Understanding, (b) Recall; no single cognitiveLevel recorded.

officialAnswer.text: (a) Griffith’s experiment. Two strains of Streptococcus pneumoniae- Smooth Virulent Strain (S-III) and Rough Avirulent Strain (R-II). R-II were injected into mice- mice remained healthy. S-III were injected into mice; mice developed pneumonia and died. S-III were heated to 60°C and killed. These heat-killed bacteria were injected to mice; mice remained healthy. A mixture of R-II and heat killed S-III bacteria were injected into mice; mice developed pneumonia and died. Conclusion: Heat killed S-III bacteria introduced some transforming principle that caused transformation of R-II avirulent into virulent S-III bacteria. (b) A- Promoter; B Coding /Anti template /Sense strand
